about.description: Seed is a comprehensive network diagnostics and monitoring tool by Mustard Seed Networks, designed to provide deep visibility into your network infrastructure.

openSource.description: Seed is source-available software (BUSL-1.1). Customize thresholds, configure tests, and integrate with your existing monitoring infrastructure.

dashboard.title: Dashboard Overview
dashboard.description: The main dashboard shows all diagnostic cards. Each card displays real-time information about a specific aspect of your network.

interface.title: Select Network Interface
interface.description: Use the interface dropdown in the header to select which network interface to monitor (e.g., eth0, wlan0). Click "Settings" to configure interface-specific options.

thresholds.title: Configure Thresholds
thresholds.description: Open Settings → Thresholds to customize warning and critical levels for DNS latency, gateway ping, Wi-Fi signal strength, and more.

runTests.title: Run Tests
runTests.description: Click the "Run All Tests" button (⚡) in the bottom right to execute speed tests, cable diagnostics, network discovery, and custom health checks.

tips.0: Use the Network Discovery card to find all devices on your network
tips.2: Export diagnostics data for troubleshooting or documentation

linkStatus.description: Monitors the physical layer connection of your network interface.

carrier.description: Physical layer signal detection. Shows 'Connected' when NIC detects a link partner (cable connected to active port).

speed.description: Negotiated link speed between your network interface and the connected device (e.g., 1000 Mbps).

duplex.description: Communication mode - Full duplex allows simultaneous bidirectional data, Half duplex is one direction at a time.

autoNeg.description: Whether speed and duplex were auto-negotiated with the link partner or manually configured.

mtu.description: Maximum Transmission Unit - largest packet size (in bytes) that can be sent without fragmentation. Standard is 1500 bytes.

cableTest.description: Time Domain Reflectometry tests cable quality and detects faults.

tdrTest.description: Sends electrical pulses through the cable and measures reflections to detect faults and measure length.

cableStatus.description: Shows if cable pairs are OK, open (disconnected), short (wires touching), or have impedance mismatch.

faultDistance.description: Distance to cable fault in meters. Helps locate physical cable problems.

pairs.description: Ethernet cables have 4 twisted pairs. Gigabit uses all 4; Fast Ethernet uses pairs 1-2 and 3-6.

cableTest.note: Cable testing requires compatible network hardware. Not all NICs support TDR.

wifiStatus.description: Monitor wireless connection quality and settings.

ssid.description: Service Set Identifier - the name of the wireless network you're connected to.

bssid.description: Basic Service Set Identifier - MAC address of the access point.

signal.description: Signal strength in dBm. -30 is excellent, -67 is good, -70 is fair, -80 is weak. Higher (less negative) is better.

channel.description: Wi-Fi channel number (1-14 for 2.4GHz, 36-165 for 5GHz). Overlapping channels cause interference.

security.description: Encryption protocol protecting the connection (WPA2, WPA3, WEP, or Open).

frequency.description: Radio band - 2.4GHz has better range, 5GHz has better speed and less interference.

networkDhcp.description: Shows IP configuration and DHCP lease information.

leaseTime.description: Duration of current IP address assignment before renewal is needed.

dhcpServer.description: IP address of the DHCP server that issued the lease (usually your router).

gateway.description: Default gateway assigned by DHCP for routing traffic off-subnet.

dnsServers.description: DNS servers assigned by DHCP for name resolution.

subnetMask.description: Network mask defining the local subnet size.

gatewayHelp.description: Tests reachability and latency to your default gateway.

ipv4Gateway.description: Default router for IPv4 traffic leaving your local network.

ipv6Gateway.description: Default router for IPv6 traffic (may be link-local address).

reachability.description: Whether the gateway responds to ICMP ping requests.

latency.description: Round-trip time to gateway. Should be <1ms for local networks.

packetLoss.description: Percentage of ping packets that didn't receive a response.

dnsTests.description: Tests DNS resolution performance and functionality.

forwardLookup.description: Resolves hostname to IPv4 address (A record).

reverseLookup.description: Resolves IP address back to hostname (PTR record).

ipv6Lookup.description: Resolves hostname to IPv6 address (AAAA record).

latency.description: Time taken for the DNS query to complete. Good: <50ms for local DNS.

performanceTests.description: Run speed tests to measure network throughput.

internetSpeed.description: Tests download/upload speeds to public speedtest servers. Measures your connection to the internet.

lanSpeed.description: Tests throughput on your local network using iperf3 to a configured server.

download.description: Maximum download speed achieved during the test.

upload.description: Maximum upload speed achieved during the test.

latency.description: Round-trip time (ping) to the test server.

jitter.description: Variation in latency over time. Lower is better for real-time applications like VoIP and gaming.

networkDiscovery.description: Discover all devices on your network and identify connected switches.

networkScan.description: Discovers active devices on your network subnet using ARP/ICMP ping sweeps.

macAddress.description: Hardware address of the network interface - unique identifier for the device.

vendor.description: Manufacturer identified from the MAC address OUI (first 3 bytes).

hostname.description: DNS hostname if reverse lookup succeeded.

lldpCdp.description: Link Layer Discovery Protocol (standard) or Cisco Discovery Protocol - provides information about directly connected network switches.

healthChecks.description: Monitor endpoint availability with automated ping, TCP, and HTTP checks.

pingTest.description: Sends ICMP echo requests to verify host reachability. Returns latency and packet loss metrics.

tcpTest.description: Attempts TCP handshake to specified port. Verifies service is accepting connections.

httpTest.description: Performs full HTTP request including DNS, TCP, TLS, and response time measurements.

customTargets.description: Configure your own endpoints to monitor in Settings → Health Checks. Add internal servers, cloud services, or critical infrastructure.

thresholds.description: Set warning (yellow) and critical (red) thresholds for latency. Configure in Settings → Thresholds.

commonIssues.title: Common Issues
commonIssues.timeout: Timeout indicates host unreachable, firewall blocking, or network path issue.
commonIssues.highLatency: High latency may indicate network congestion, routing issues, or overloaded server.
commonIssues.packetLoss: Packet loss suggests network congestion, faulty equipment, or wireless interference.
commonIssues.connectionRefused: Connection refused means the service is not running or listening on that port.

security.description: Security features including device scanning, vulnerability detection, and password management.

portScan.description: Identifies open network ports on discovered devices. Helps detect unauthorized services or security risks.

vulnScan.description: Checks devices for known vulnerabilities based on detected services, versions, and CVE databases.

devicePosture.description: Assesses security posture of network devices including open ports, outdated services, and misconfigurations.

rogueDhcp.description: Detects unauthorized DHCP servers on the network that could intercept traffic or assign malicious configurations.

passwordRecovery.title: Password Recovery

steps.0: SSH into the server running Seed
steps.1: Create an empty file named '.recovery' in the data directory
steps.4: The server will detect the file and generate a recovery token
steps.5: Read the token from '.recovery-token' in the same directory
steps.6: Enter the token on the login page along with your new password
steps.7: The token expires after 15 minutes and is single-use

passwordRecovery.note: This requires filesystem access to the server, proving you have admin-level access to the machine.

noCarrier.description: Check the cable at both ends, the switch power and port, and whether the interface is enabled. Try another cable or port.

slowSpeed.symptom: Link speed lower than expected (100Mbps instead of 1Gbps)
slowSpeed.description: Check the cable category and all four pairs, switch capabilities, and speed/duplex negotiation.

open.description: A wire is disconnected or broken. Check terminations and the reported distance to the fault.

short.description: Two wires are touching. Check the connector pins and inspect the cable for damage.

unreachable.description: Verify the configured gateway address and local link. A gateway may block ICMP even when forwarding traffic.

slowInternet.description: Compare wired and wireless results, test at another time, and compare LAN throughput with internet throughput.

profiles.description: Profiles allow you to save and switch between different configuration sets for different clients, locations, or testing scenarios.

clientSpecific.title: Client-Specific Settings
clientSpecific.description: Each profile can have unique thresholds, health check targets, SNMP credentials, and discovery settings tailored to that environment.

quickSwitch.title: Quick Profile Switching
quickSwitch.description: Switch between profiles instantly from the header dropdown. All settings are applied immediately without restart.

exportImport.title: Export & Import
exportImport.description: Export profiles as JSON files to share between devices or backup configurations. Import profiles from other Seed installations.

defaultProfile.title: Default Profile
defaultProfile.description: One profile can be marked as default and will be automatically loaded on startup.

tips.0: Use descriptive profile names that identify the client and location
tips.1: Create a baseline 'Default' profile with standard settings
tips.2: Export profiles before major changes as a backup

rtspChecks.description: Monitor RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) endpoints for IP camera and video surveillance systems.

rtspUrl.description: The address of the RTSP stream, typically in format rtsp://host:port/path. Port 554 is the standard RTSP port.

options.description: An RTSP command that queries the server for supported methods. Used as a lightweight connectivity check.

describe.description: Requests media description (SDP) from the server. Verifies the stream exists and is accessible.

authentication.description: RTSP servers typically require username/password. Supports Basic and Digest authentication methods.

steps.0: Go to Settings → Health Checks → RTSP Endpoints
steps.6: Enable the endpoint to start monitoring

dicomChecks.description: Monitor DICOM medical imaging systems including CT, MRI, ultrasound, and PACS servers.

aeTitle.description: Application Entity Title - a unique identifier (up to 16 characters) that identifies a DICOM node. Both calling (local) and called (remote) AE Titles must be configured correctly.

cEcho.description: DICOM verification service. Sends a 'ping' to verify the remote DICOM node is reachable and responding. Returns success/failure status.

association.description: A DICOM connection between two nodes. Both AE Titles must be registered in each other's configuration for associations to succeed.

scp.description: The DICOM server that provides services (e.g., PACS, modality worklist). The target of your health check.

scu.description: The DICOM client requesting services. Seed acts as an SCU when performing C-ECHO tests.

port.description: Standard DICOM port is 104, but many systems use 11112 or custom ports. Verify with your PACS administrator.

points.0: C-ECHO is a non-destructive verification - it doesn't access patient data
points.3: Coordinate AE Title registration with your biomedical/IT team

howTo.description: Step-by-step guides for common tasks and troubleshooting scenarios.

diagnoseSlowNetwork.title: How to Diagnose Slow Network Speeds

0.description: Verify the Link Status card shows expected speed (1 Gbps for gigabit). If showing 100 Mbps, check cable quality or switch port.

1.description: Gateway latency should be <1ms for wired connections. High latency here indicates local network issues.

2.description: Compare results to your ISP's advertised speeds. If significantly lower, the issue may be ISP-related.

3.description: Test local network throughput to isolate whether the issue is local or internet-bound. Should achieve near wire speed.

4.description: For Wi-Fi, check the channel graph and neighbor AP scan for congestion and interference.

setupHealthChecks.title: How to Configure Health Checks for Critical Services

0.description: List all services that need monitoring: servers, databases, cloud services, cameras, medical equipment.

1.description: Use Ping for basic reachability, TCP for service ports, HTTP for web services, RTSP for cameras, DICOM for medical imaging.

2.description: Go to Settings → Health Checks and add each endpoint with appropriate parameters.

3.description: Configure warning (yellow) and critical (red) latency thresholds based on service requirements.

4.description: Run tests manually first to verify connectivity before enabling continuous monitoring.

5.description: Ensure settings are saved to the appropriate client profile for persistence.

wifiTroubleshooting.description: Inspect visible access points, channels, signal and noise to diagnose the local wireless environment. Available measurements depend on the adapter and platform.

neighbors.description: Lists access points the adapter can hear, with their SSID, BSSID, band, channel and signal level.

utilization.description: The reported channel activity indicates how busy the channel is. Missing measurements do not establish an idle channel.

interference.description: Access points on the same channel share airtime, which can reduce throughput.

snr.description: Signal is measured in dBm; SNR compares the signal with background noise. Higher SNR generally indicates a cleaner link.

path.description: Trace the route to a destination and inspect devices discovered on the local network. Missing replies are not proof that every intermediate device is offline.

hop.description: A responding step along the route, with round-trip latency and any available hostname.

protocol.description: Choose the probe protocol for the trace. Firewalls and routers may handle ICMP, UDP and TCP differently.

local.description: ARP and neighbor discovery reveal reachable neighbors on the local segment.

reports.description: Review service availability and generate or download diagnostic reports. Available actions depend on your role and license.

sla.description: Availability and latency summaries come from recorded health checks. Review the time window and data coverage before interpreting them.

export.description: Generate a report from collected diagnostics or download an existing report. An operator role is required for writes.

logs.description: Review structured log entries and the health of the Seed process. Filter logs by level, source or text to investigate a failed test.

level.description: Severity such as debug, info, warning or error. A filter narrows the displayed entries.

source.description: The component that emitted the entry, such as discovery or Wi-Fi.

stream.description: Pause or resume the displayed stream and export entries for investigation.

alerts.description: Review conditions raised by monitoring, then filter by severity and acknowledgment or resolution state. Your signed-in identity is recorded when you acknowledge an alert.

severity.description: Indicates the urgency of the observed condition.

ack.description: Mark the alert as seen while keeping it open for investigation.

resolve.description: Mark the alert as resolved after verifying the condition has been addressed.

pollingTargets.description: Add, edit or remove devices monitored over SNMP. A new target starts on the next polling cycle. Discovered devices and links feed Topology; observed changes can raise alerts.

target.description: A device address that Seed polls at a recurring interval.

collectors.description: Collectors read supported system, interface, LLDP, ARP and forwarding-table data from a target.

snmp.description: Simple Network Management Protocol reads device state and tables using the configured credentials.

topology.description: Inspect the network graph assembled from discovery and SNMP polling. Select a node to review its interfaces and observed links. A missing link can indicate missing observations.

node.description: A discovered device such as a switch, router, host or access point.

link.description: An observed relationship between device interfaces, reconciled from discovery data.

interface.description: A device port with its status and any observed neighbors.

arp.description: Address Resolution Protocol maps IPv4 addresses to local MAC addresses.

dhcp.description: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol assigns network configuration to clients.

dns.description: Domain Name System resolves names to addresses and supports reverse lookups.

iperf.description: A tool for measuring throughput between two network hosts.

lldp.description: Discovery protocols that report information about directly connected devices.

rtsp.description: Real Time Streaming Protocol is used by cameras and video systems.

snr.description: Signal-to-noise ratio compares a wireless signal with background noise.

tdr.description: Time Domain Reflectometry estimates cable length and locates faults using reflected pulses.

LinkCard.description: Link state, negotiated speed and addressing for the selected wired interface.

CableCard.description: Cable diagnostics appear when the wired link is down and require an adapter that supports TDR.

DriverStatsCard.description: Driver counters can expose errors and drops. Platforms without the required driver support report that limitation.

WiFiCard.description: Inspect the connected network, signal and security details. Operating-system privacy restrictions can withhold identifiers; a withheld SSID is not proof of disconnection.

NetworkCard.description: Review addresses, DHCP lease and interface configuration.

GatewayCard.description: Check the default gateway and its measured reachability and latency.

DnsCard.description: Inspect configured resolvers and the results of forward, reverse and IPv6 lookups.

NeighbourCacheCard.description: Inspect the operating system’s IPv4 ARP and IPv6 neighbor cache. Entries describe observed neighbors, not a complete device inventory.

BonjourCard.description: Browse services advertised through mDNS and DNS-SD, with their hosts and ports. Missing advertisements do not prove a service is offline.

PublicIpCard.description: Review the externally observed address and its history when public-IP checks are available.

SwitchCard.description: On wired interfaces, inspect switch-neighbor and VLAN information when the connected device advertises it.

PathDiscoveryCard.description: Run a trace to a destination and inspect the responding hops and their latency.

NetworkDiscoveryCard.description: Scan configured local networks and inspect discovered devices, addresses and advertised services.

WiFiChannelGraph.description: Compare visible AP signals by channel. Failed or privacy-restricted scans cannot establish an empty airspace.

WiFiAirspaceCard.description: Inspect APs and stations observed in management-frame capture. Requires the licensed capability and a monitor-capable capture source.

WiFiAnomaliesCard.description: Review association anomalies from captured management frames. Without capture observations there is no basis to declare the environment healthy.

MfaCard.description: Set up an authenticator app (TOTP), keep recovery codes safely, or register a passkey when your browser supports it. Confirm enrollment before relying on the second factor.

GuestNetworkAuditCard.description: Check configured guest-network isolation targets. Test only networks you are authorized to assess.

InsecurePortScanCard.description: Scan the configured target for exposed insecure services and inspect the findings before taking action.

BluetoothCard.description: Inspect nearby Bluetooth devices when the host adapter and platform support discovery. An unavailable adapter is not an empty scan.

HealthCheckCard.description: Run configured ping, TCP, UDP and application checks. HTTP timing segments separate DNS, connection, TLS, server response and download time; focus each segment label for its explanation.

PerformanceCard.description: Compare internet speed tests with LAN iperf3 results to locate a throughput bottleneck. Both endpoints and link conditions affect the result.

SlaDashboardCard.description: Review availability and latency over the selected reporting window, including gaps in observations.

ReportsCard.description: Generate, download or remove reports according to your role. Review their data window before sharing them.

SystemHealthCard.description: Inspect the Seed process and host resource measurements while investigating slow or failed tests.

LogViewerCard.description: Search, pause and export structured log entries to investigate daemon activity.

thresholds.dnsLookup: Time to resolve hostnames. Good: <50ms for local DNS, <100ms for public DNS. Warning indicates potential resolver issues.
thresholds.gatewayPing: Round-trip time to your default gateway (router). Good: <20ms for local LAN. High latency suggests network congestion or equipment issues.
thresholds.wifiSignal: Signal strength in dBm (negative values). Good: >-50 (excellent), Warning: >-70 (good), below -70 is weak. Higher (less negative) is better.
thresholds.healthCheckPing: ICMP ping latency to configured targets. Adjust based on target distance - local servers should be <50ms, internet hosts may be higher.
thresholds.healthCheckTcp: TCP connection time to configured ports. Includes SYN-ACK round trip. Good: <100ms for local services.
thresholds.httpTotal: Total time for complete HTTP request including DNS, TCP, TLS, and response. Good: <500ms for simple pages.
thresholds.httpDns: DNS resolution phase of HTTP request. Should be fast if using local resolver or cached results.
thresholds.httpTcp: TCP handshake time within HTTP request. High values indicate network latency or congestion.
thresholds.httpTls: TLS/SSL handshake time. Includes certificate exchange and key negotiation. Affected by cipher strength.
thresholds.httpTtfb: Time to First Byte - server processing time. High values indicate slow backend or database queries.
